<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.

### Common mistakes to avoid:

**Mistake 1: Bare comma-separated atoms without a head.**
```
WRONG:  input(BR, BC, V), V != 0.
RIGHT:  nonzero(BR, BC, V) :- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0.
```

**Mistake 2: Assignment without a head predicate.**
```
WRONG:  offset1 = BR + BC.
RIGHT:  offset1(O) :- O = BR + BC, input(BR, BC, _).
```

**Mistake 3: Putting aggregate on the left of `=`.**
```
WRONG:  #min{R : input(R,_,_)} = Rmin.
RIGHT:  Rmin = #min{R : input(R,_,_)}.
```

**Mistake 4: Unsafe variables (variables not grounded in a positive predicate).**
```
WRONG:  col_nonzero(C) :- #count{R : input(R,C,V), V != 0} > 0.
RIGHT:  col_nonzero(C) :- input(_, C, _), #count{R : input(R,C,V), V != 0} > 0.
```

**Mistake 5: Using `#mod` instead of `\`.**
```
WRONG:  even(C) :- C #mod 2 = 0.
RIGHT:  even(C) :- C \ 2 = 0.
```

**Mistake 6: Using `aggregate/3` (SWI-Prolog syntax).**
```
WRONG:  row_five_count(R, N) :- aggregate(N = #count, input(R,_,5), N).
RIGHT:  row_five_count(R, N) :- N = #count{C : input(R,C,5)}.
```

Use `#show output/3.` at the end of your program so Clingo only prints the output predicate.
</rules>

Below is one worked example, followed by a reusable template.

<example_1>
This puzzle copies all non-zero cells from input to output and removes cells with color 0.

<example_grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</example_grid_1>

<example_grid_2>
Input:
<diagram>
0 0 0
0 0 5
0 0 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 0 0
0 0 5
0 0 0
</diagram>
</example_grid_2>

<transformation>
The output is identical to the input: every cell keeps its original color.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).
</asp>
</example_1>

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Determine the top‑leftmost non‑zero cell (the start cell)
rows_nonzero(R) :- #count{C : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0} > 0.
start_r(R0) :- #min{R : rows_nonzero(R)}.

start_c(C0) :- input(start_r(start_r), C0, _), start_r(start_r) = #min{R : #count{C : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0} > 0}, Color != 0, C0 = #min{C : input(start_r(start_r), C, _), Color != 0}.

% The colour of the start cell – this is the colour we have to keep
outer_color_val(O) :- input(start_r(start_r), start_c(start_c), O).

% A cell may be traversed only if it is either the outer colour or empty
allowed(R,C) :- outer_color_val(O), input(R, C, O), input(R, C, 0).

% Reachable cells from the start cell (4‑directional flood fill)
reachable(R0, C0) :- start_r(R0), start_c(C0).
reachable(R, C) :- reachable(Rp, Cp), R = Rp+1, C = Cp, allowed(R, C).
reachable(R, C) :- reachable(Rp, Cp), R = Rp-1, C = Cp, allowed(R, C).
reachable(R, C) :- reachable(Rp, Cp), R = Rp, C = Cp+1, allowed(R, C).
reachable(R, C) :- reachable(Rp, Cp), R = Rp, C = Cp-1, allowed(R, C).

% Output: reachable cells get the outer colour, other cells are zero
output(R, C, O)   :- output_cell(R, C), reachable(R, C), outer_color_val(O).
output(R, C, 0)   :- output_cell(R, C), not reachable(R, C).

% Each output cell must obtain exactly one colour
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Constraints
:- output(R, C, Color), output_cell(R, C), reachable(R, C), outer_color_val(O), Color != outer_color_val(O).
:- output(R, C, Color), output_cell(R, C), not reachable(R, C), Color != 0.

% Show the result
#show output/3.

% Count each non‑zero colour
cnt(C,N) :- N = #count{C2 : input(R, C2, C), C != 0}.

% Max count among colours
max_count(M) :- M = #max{C : cnt(C,N)}.

% Primary colour – the most frequent non‑zero colour
primary_colour(P) :- cnt(P,N), max_count(M), N = M, P != 0.

% Secondary colour – the other non‑zero colour
secondary_colour(S) :- colour(S), S != 0, primary_colour(P), S != P,
    S = #min{T : colour(T), T != 0, T != P}.

% Row and column limits
rows_max(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
cols_max(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.
row(R)   :- rows_max(N), R = 0..N-1.
col(C)   :- cols_max(M), C = 0..M-1.
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Adjacent cells (4‑directional)
neighbor(R,R2,C2) :- (R2 = R+1, C2 = C).
neighbor(R,R2,C2) :- (R2 = R-1, C2 = C).
neighbor(R,R2,C2) :- (R2 = R,   C2 = C+1).
neighbor(R,R2,C2) :- (R2 = R,   C2 = C-1).

% Border cells of the primary colour (adjacent to a different colour or zero)
border(R,C) :- primary_colour(P), input(R,C,P),
    #count{R2,C2 : neighbor(R,R2,C2), input(R2,C2,Col), Col != P} > 0.

% Output constraints
:- output(R,C,Colour), not border(R,C), Colour != 0.
:- output(R,C,Colour), border(R,C), Colour != secondary_colour(S), secondary_colour(S).

% Exactly one colour per cell
1 { output(R,C,Colour) : colour(Colour) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

```
WRONG:  input(BR, BC, V), V != 0.
RIGHT:  nonzero(BR, BC, V) :- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0.
```

**Mistake 2: Assignment without a head predicate.**
```
WRONG:  offset1 = BR + BC.
RIGHT:  offset1(O) :- O = BR + BC, input(BR, BC, _).
```

**Mistake 3: Putting aggregate on the left of `=`.**
```
WRONG:  #min{R : input(R,_,_)} = Rmin.
RIGHT:  Rmin = #min{R : input(R,_,_)}.
```

**Mistake 4: Unsafe variables (variables not grounded in a positive predicate).**
```
WRONG:  col_nonzero(C) :- #count{R : input(R,C,V), V != 0} > 0.
RIGHT:  col_nonzero(C) :- input(_, C, _), #count{R : input(R,C,V), V != 0} > 0.
```

**Mistake 5: Using `#mod` instead of `\`.**
```
WRONG:  even(C) :- C #mod 2 = 0.
RIGHT:  even(C) :- C \ 2 = 0.
```

**Mistake 6: Using `aggregate/3` (SWI-Prolog syntax).**
```
WRONG:  row_five_count(R, N) :- aggregate(N = #count, input(R,_,5), N).
RIGHT:  row_five_count(R, N) :- N = #count{C : input(R,C,5)}.
```

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.
row(R) :- R = 0..N-1.
col(C) :- C = 0..M-1.

% Cells with at least one non‑zero value
rows_nonzero(R) :- input(R, _, _), #count{C : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0} > 0.

% Top‑leftmost non‑zero cell (start)
R0 = #min{R : rows_nonzero(R)}.
C0 = #min{C : input(R0, C, Color), Color != 0}.

% Colour of the start cell (the outer colour)
outer_color_val(O) :- input(R0, C0, O).

% Allowed cells for the flood fill (outer colour or zero)
allowed(R, C) :- outer_color_val(O), input(R, C, O).
allowed(R, C) :- outer_color_val(O), input(R, C, 0).

% Flood fill (4‑directional)
reachable(R0, C0) :- true.
reachable(R, C) :- reachable(Rp, Cp), R = Rp+1, allowed(R, C).
reachable(R, C) :- reachable(Rp, Cp), R = Rp-1, allowed(R, C).
reachable(R, C) :- reachable(Rp, Cp), C = Cp+1, allowed(R, C).

% Count each non-zero color
cnt(C,N) :- N = #count{C2 : input(R, C2, C), C != 0}.

% Max count among colors
max_count(M) :- M = #max{C : cnt(C,N)}.

% Primary color (most frequent non‑zero color)
primary_color_val(P) :- cnt(P,N), max_count(M), N = M, P != 0.

% Secondary color (other non‑zero color)
secondary_color(S) :- color(S), S != 0, primary_color_val(P), S != P,
                      S = #min{T : color(T), T != 0, T != P}.

% Row and column limits
rows_max(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
cols_max(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.
row(R) :- rows_max(N), R = 0..N-1.
col(C) :- cols_max(M), C = 0..M-1.
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Neighbor relation (4‑directional)
neighbor(R,R2,C2) :- (R2 = R+1, C2 = C).
neighbor(R,R2,C2) :- (R2 = R-1, C2 = C).
neighbor(R,R2,C2) :- (R2 = R, C2 = C+1).
neighbor(R,R2,C2) :- (R2 = R, C2 = C-1).

% Border cells of the primary colour
border(R,C) :- primary_color_val(P), input(R,C,P),
    #count{R2,C2 : neighbor(R,R2,C2), input(R2,C2,Col), Col != P} > 0.

% Exact one colour per output cell (border -> secondary, else zero)
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color),
      (border(R,C), secondary_color(S), Color = S) ;
